entity.name: Yash Bavadiya
entity.description: Yash Bavadiya is the creator and maintainer of Breakscale, an open source system design simulator used for teaching how distributed systems behave under load. He maintains the discrete-event engine, the component library, the worked examples, the test suite and the contributor workflow.

projects.name: Breakscale
projects.description: Breakscale is an MIT-licensed system design simulator that runs the diagram instead of drawing it. A student places components on a canvas, pushes traffic through them, and watches real queueing behaviour emerge: latency percentiles climbing, queues filling, circuit breakers tripping and retry storms collapsing a system that was healthy a moment earlier. Every number comes from a discrete-event simulation rather than a formula, and vendor pricing is cited from published rates with the date it was read, because a teaching tool that shows a plausible number is worse than one that shows none. It ships 33 component types, 23 worked examples and a 100 term glossary, and runs entirely in the browser with no account and no backend. Funding would support per-example teaching pages, accessibility work, the traffic scenario controls, and time spent reviewing contributions.
